When an AI model says gold will rise, anyone can score the call at the close, but few can check when it was made. A backtest mixes memory with skill, and an operator's log asks for trust. I propose a standard for measuring AI market forecasts, written as a ladder of checkable requirements, and I run its reference implementation, AI Council · Markets: an open league where fourteen models, seven from US and seven from Chinese laboratories, face one question on one price snapshot. Before each New York open the ten on its Council, five from each side, give probabilities for twelve indicators at four horizons. Each answer is sealed into a hash chain before the price it is scored from, the chain is anchored in Bitcoin and signed by independent time-stamping authorities, and one run per session counts by a rule declared in advance. On 21 October 2026, the first counted morning, every counted answer was signed before the 09:30 ET open. Agreement among the models proved to be a count of independent voices, not a headcount: on two development mornings the seven and eight models sealed before the open were as alike as about 1.6 independent forecasters, nine counted ones were worth 2.23, and the closest pairs crossed the US-China line. items.summary: Large organizations increasingly face what this book calls the cognitive complexity wall: at the scale of hundreds of interacting components, maintaining the dependency map and reacting at the pace of incidents exceeds what a human team can deliver. This conceptual volume proposes AAM/5C, in which five capabilities (Capture, Comprehend, Choose, Coordinate, Control) are instantiated across seven logical layers, L1 to L7. A single authorization rule, R-AUT, separates who proposes, who decides and who executes: a probabilistic planner (L4) proposes; a governance layer (L6) decides under signed policies and records its verdict in a signed evaluation proof; a security layer (L5) issues a short-lived act token bound to that proof; a policy enforcement point verifies both before the target layer materializes the act. Under an explicit guarantee contract, two analytical statements (H7a, H8a) hold by construction. The other statements of its ten hypotheses (H1 to H10), including log completeness (H7b) and non-bypass of the enforcement point (H8b), are refutable, and the protocol that could refute them is fixed before any measurement. The contribution of the book is a prescriptive reference model that articulates, under this single authorization rule, known mechanisms and adds three constructs, all to be validated: the Validation step of the Distributed Autonomy Loop, the ephemeral authority surface and the cognitive dependency plane. The book positions them against autonomic computing, multi-agent systems, enterprise architecture and agent protocols (MCP, A2A), gives an authorization policy in Rego and a partial TLA+ specification of peer consensus, and sets out a validation program with quantified milestones. It reports no empirical results. This English edition is a translation of the French original, produced with the assistance of AI tools and validated by the author.
items.title: Agentic Architecture of Information Systems. The AAM/5C Model: A Reference Model for Distributed Autonomy

items.summary: Sixth-generation (6G) communication systems are expected to support immersive, intent-driven, and latency-critical services through tight integration of multimodal intelligence, edge computing, and autonomous network control. In this setting, agentic AI systems can reason over heterogeneous inputs, use tools and network functions, coordinate across distributed entities, and adapt to dynamic environments. These capabilities make agentic multimodal intelligence promising for 6G applications such as semantic communications, digital twins, and zero-touch network management, but they also introduce security and privacy risks that extend beyond conventional AI and network security models. Vulnerabilities can propagate across multimodal data pipelines, memory, tools, communication interfaces, and inter-agent coordination loops. We survey multimodal intelligence and agentic AI for 6G cross-layered communication systems from the perspectives of privacy and security. We present a 6G-oriented system view spanning perception, memory, tool use, and multi-agent orchestration; analyze threat models and attack surfaces across sensing, cognition, action, memory, and communication layers; organize existing attacks into a structured taxonomy; and review mitigation strategies including prompt and memory defenses, inter-agent trust mechanisms, secure orchestration, and privacy-preserving learning. We conclude by outlining open research directions for trustworthy multimodal multi-agent 6G systems.
items.title: Secure Agentic AI and Multimodal Intelligence in 6G Communication Systems

items.summary: Multi-task generalization is an important yet underexplored problem in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Many real-world applications require multi-agent systems to generalize across complex, temporally extended tasks with diverse inter-agent coordination requirements. We introduce a specification language that combines temporal-logic task specifications with operators for expressing such requirements. We propose SpecMAGIC, a hierarchical framework that leverages the automaton structure of task specifications for subtask decomposition. A centralized high-level planner identifies and allocates compatible subtask sequences across agents, while decentralized low-level policies execute individual subtasks. This enables zero-shot generalization to new tasks by composing reusable subtask policies according to new specifications, without retraining. We establish soundness and probabilistic completeness of the high-level planner. Experiments on multi-agent navigation tasks show that SpecMAGIC substantially outperforms existing approaches on unseen task specifications and maintains strong performance as the number of agents increases.
items.title: SpecMAGIC: Specification-Guided Multi-Task Generalization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models

items.summary: This paper develops the Phase Compatibility branch of Harmonic Physics: a framework for examining how physical participants enter constrained phase relations, produce collective outcomes, and form persistent higher-level organisations capable of further recursive participation. Building on established synchronization theory, phase locking, coupled-oscillator dynamics and phasor mathematics, the framework examines reinforcement, opposition, cancellation, reshaping and whole formation. It distinguishes mathematical admissibility, actual source occupancy, participant admission, active interaction, closure, continuing identity and observation. A compatibility basin is characterised through maintained relational organisation and persistence under declared conditions. Version 3.1 aligns the shared definitions with the current Foundations and Observer Theory papers, corrects the amplitude-weighted moment family, and clarifies the distinction between passive changes of representation and physical projection or coupling. It incorporates the completed mathematical nesting construction, which preserves a supplied quantum state’s amplitude and relative-phase information, together with Born probabilities under corresponding joint measurements. Phase Theory Equations is identified as the consolidated reference for the current mathematical expressions. The observation account separates source organisation, information encoded into light, receiver coupling, registration, retention and calibrated reconstruction. Within the proposed optical terminology, light performs the observer role through source–receiver coupling, while the receiver registers and retains a physical response. Minimal relational consciousness and awareness retain separate definitions. The paper integrates controlled models, molecular spectral studies, a superconducting-qubit analogue, simulated liquid-water reorganisation, quantum-state encoding and specified receiver models, preserving the scope and limitations of each result. It sets out the state spaces, conservation requirements, comparison models and prospective failure conditions required for physical applications. Universal participant-admission and whole-formation laws remain open research questions; this revision introduces no new experimental validation.
items.title: Phase Compatibility: Harmonic Combination, Selective Participation, Whole Formation, and Recursive Organisation

items.summary: The limited communication resources and sensing perspectives of a single uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) motivate UAV swarms for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in air-ground networks. However, in multi-region scenarios, regional UAV allocations may not match vehicle demand, while local observations may lack sufficient diversity for accurate sensing. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cross-region cooperation framework for UAV swarms. For communication, cross-region UAV reallocation reduces service disparities by matching resources to vehicle demand. For sensing, combining UAV observations from different regions increases observation diversity, while adaptive handshaking guided by marginal Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) utilities balances phase synchronization gains against handshaking energy consumption. Joint optimization of UAV positions and transmit power within each region then further improves communication service and sensing performance. These coupled decisions are coordinated by a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (H-MARL) approach through slow-timescale inter-region UAV reallocation and fast-timescale intra-region UAV control. Under the considered simulation settings, reallocation can improve quality of service (QoS) by over 20 percentage points compared with retaining the initial allocation under severe resource-demand mismatches. Cooperative sensing with adaptive handshaking incurs only about a 5.0% increase in mean CRB relative to perfect synchronization.
items.title: Cross-Region Cooperation of UAV Swarms Towards Air-Ground ISAC via Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

items.summary: LLM-based scam systems increasingly combine adaptive dialogue, persistent context, external tools, and multi-agent coordination to automate personalized fraud. These capabilities also create a resource dependency: every reasoning step, model call, and coordination round incurs inference cost. We present TokenTrap, a resource-oriented defense that redirects suspected scam systems toward benign, low-value computation while withholding credentials, payments, and other exploitable information. TokenTrap combines three components: an architecture-specific token-task library, a router that selects among single-agent, hierarchical, and flat multi-agent workflows, and a bounded anti-guardrail strategy that varies task presentation while enforcing token, round, time, and safety limits. Across 50-round traces, TokenTrap amplifies token consumption by $2{,}487.0\times$, $1{,}616.0\times$, and $567.8\times$ relative to a no-token-task baseline for the three workflows. Its router achieves 85.67% accuracy on 300 architecture-labeled prompts. These results demonstrate that short, non-sensitive requests can impose substantial context-processing and coordination costs, motivating resource-aware defense as a complement to scam detection.
items.title: Your Token Is Gone: A Token-Consumption Countermeasure for Disrupting LLM-Based Scam Systems

items.summary: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
items.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions

items.summary: RFT-FaultBench provides training-process telemetry for anomaly detection and failure-type diagnosis in reinforcement fine-tuning. This revised dataset contains 2,630 runs (339 normal and 2,291 injected), 72,100 train-step records, and 2,617,600 training trajectories across OpenRLHF, AgentEvolver, and TRL and five task categories: arithmetic reasoning, GSM8K-style mathematical reasoning, code generation, verifiable instruction following, and tool calling. It includes 55 compound-failure runs for detection; diagnosis uses 2,236 single-failure runs. Task versions and native failure-label coverage differ across frameworks. The package includes run-level artifacts, canonical labels and seeds, five seed-grouped evaluation folds, 25 one-shot support draws, provenance and exclusion ledgers, per-file checksums, and Python example loaders and validation tools. Membership follows the frozen 2026-10-12 evaluation snapshot. It updates the earlier 779-run release; no new training was performed during packaging. GitHub companion: AIOps4LLM/RFT-FaultBench . Related manuscript: Towards Robust LLM Post-Training: Automatic Failure Diagnosis for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning. Extract RFT-FaultBench-full.tar.gz and consult its README and docs for schemas, verification evidence, and evaluation scope. The dataset continues the CC BY 4.0 license of the preceding Zenodo version.

items.summary: We study intransitive probabilistic preferences through dice whose face labels may be repeated. We distinguish restricted models, in which the set of permitted labels depends on the number of sides, from the unrestricted model, which allows arbitrary integer labels. We review existence results, including the exceptional impossibility of a Chinese chain of five four-sided dice, and give an explicit construction establishing the known existence of simple cycles of three-sided dice of every length m ≥3, with no ties and a net win margin of one. We examine mixed-integer programming, simulated annealing, and lexicographic optimization of the margins. We then extend pairwise comparison to probability measures by means of bounded, measurable, antisymmetric kernels. For complete comparison data with uniform weights, we derive the Hodge decomposition of the margin matrix into an additive score component and an orthogonal, divergence-free residual. We distinguish the failure of an exact additive representation from the existence of strict preference cycles. The minimax theorem ensures that every finite family admits a mixed strategy with nonnegative expected margin against every mixture of that family. For the historical cycle with margins 4, 4, 10, we compute both the decomposition and the equilibrium mixture (2/9, 5/9, 2/9). Applications to portfolios, artistic evaluation, visual perception, and sports clarify the distinctions among independent comparisons, shared scenarios, and expected utility.

items.summary: Highlights of the Study This comprehensive review examines the fatigue behaviour of load-bearing polymeric bone scaffolds , addressing a critical but comparatively underexplored aspect of bone tissue engineering. It evaluates the mechanisms governing fatigue damage and systematically examines how polymer characteristics, microstructure, reinforcing materials, scaffold topology, manufacturing methods, loading conditions, body fluids, and tissue ingrowth influence fatigue performance, with particular emphasis on translating polymeric scaffolds toward reliable load-bearing clinical applications. Key findings: 🟢 Fatigue failure mechanisms: Polymeric scaffolds can undergo both mechanical and thermal fatigue. Repeated cyclic loading causes residual-strain accumulation, stiffness and peak-stress reduction, crack development, and hysteretic heating, which can progressively degrade polymer chains and ultimately cause structural failure. 🟢 Low- and high-cycle fatigue: Low-cycle fatigue generally occurs under relatively high stresses and involves repeated plastic deformation, whereas high-cycle fatigue develops over much larger numbers of cycles under lower stress levels and is primarily associated with elastic deformation and progressive material degradation. 🟢 Material and microstructural effects: Polymer fatigue resistance is strongly governed by molecular and microstructural characteristics. Increased crystallinity, molecular weight, and molecular-chain entanglement can improve fatigue resistance, emphasizing the importance of selecting and tailoring the polymer microstructure for load-bearing scaffolds. 🟢 Reinforcement strategy: Incorporating ceramic or metallic reinforcing phases can substantially improve the fatigue performance of polymeric scaffolds by redistributing applied loads and dissipating energy that would otherwise contribute to polymer deformation and heat generation. 🟢 Hydroxyapatite reinforcement: Incorporation of 15 wt% hydroxyapatite increased the fatigue limit of PLA scaffolds by approximately 17%, while also improving compressive modulus, crack resistance, and hysteresis energy compared with unreinforced PLA. 🟢 Scaffold topology: Pore architecture plays a decisive role in fatigue behaviour by controlling stress distribution and stress concentration. Even scaffolds fabricated from the same polymer and having comparable porosity can exhibit substantially different fatigue lives when their pore geometry and filament arrangement are changed. 🟢 Topology-dependent fatigue life: Among 3D-printed PLA scaffolds with comparable porosity, the tetragonal topology achieved a fatigue life of approximately 4400 cycles, outperforming hexagonal and wheel-like structures at approximately 3200 and 2500 cycles, respectively. 🟢 Advanced scaffold architectures: TPMS, Voronoi, functionally graded, auxetic, and other irregular architectures offer promising approaches for load-bearing scaffolds. The inspections dataset (207 rows) gives the most recent published inspection per facility from ICE Office of Detention Oversight reports in the ICE FOIA Library 2025–2026 listing window (179 facilities) plus the 28 facility-specific DHS Office of Inspector General detention inspection reports of fiscal years 2021–2026, with each report's published Facility Rating and deficient-standards count reproduced verbatim, never re-graded. The deaths dataset (84 rows) lists the deaths in ICE custody in ICE's Detainee Death Reporting tables for fiscal years 2021–2026, each with the ICE death report ICE itself published (name, age, country of citizenship, facility, date of death, and cause of death where the report states one). Sources: ICE FOIA Library, DHS Office of Inspector General, and ICE Detainee Death Reporting, retrieved October 23, 2026. Tool: https://inspections-ledger.straitresearch.org/. Direction and final calls by Athena Anthea; research judgment and technical execution shared with an AI assistant. Version 1.1 (October 24, 2026) adds: a published facility-name crosswalk (200 canonical facilities) with single-facility dossiers joining ODO, OIG, and deaths records per facility; an extraction naming the deficient standards behind the published counts for 52 of the 179 ODO inspection rows (validated by hand-checking 10 reports; coverage and per-row failure reasons stated, never guessed); and deaths tables showing cause stated (12) vs not stated (72) by fiscal year and facility.

items.summary: Companion software for Precision boundaries in spiking transport of recursive mixture uncertainty, by Chris Twombly (Independent researcher, Centennial, Colorado, USA). Version 1.2.0 retains the v1.0/v1.1 sources and replay/reporting packages. It adds the frozen S5 dependency source code, runtime-only twelve-worker amendment helper, a portable saved-evidence verifier and archive reporting tools. The numerical worker sources and original scientific lock are unchanged. The verifier passed all deposited-file hashes and recomputed all 960 candidate peaks at 90 digits on a clean extraction on the same computer; this is not full tracker regeneration or a second-machine replay. The separately source/seed/protocol-locked S5 campaign completed 480 independent new physical trajectories with paired healthy/fault sensing (960 streams, 256 scans), four arms (3,840 runs), and 960 high-precision audits. Its prespecified composite fidelity endpoint had 0/480 base failures; the exact one-sided 95% upper failure bound was 0.622167%, with exact p=0.00803329 at a 1% null failure rate. Every selection was the 40-bit floor. This supports the tested artificial population, not adaptive-width benefits, higher-width branches, calibration improvement or universal 40-bit sufficiency. Earlier 40-bit stress failures remain valid. Signed integrate-and-fire packets operate within a numerical host-recursive Gaussian-process mixture tracker. Host gains, weights, mixture assembly and forecast algebra remain numerical. Author code is MIT; retained third-party components keep their notices. The original pipeline retains frozen path/dependency assumptions and is not claimed fully relocatable; the portable verifier checks the saved S5 evidence without importing that pipeline. Original locks, analyses, stress breaches and failed endpoints are retained. The independent-machine R1 replay remains not passed (7/8). S5 is fresh synthetic confirmation, not another independent-machine replay. Cross-platform regeneration previously agreed within 5e-11 rather than bitwise; saved synthetic inputs remain the numerical reference. External-data exclusions are unchanged: no K-Radar data/derived outcomes, TartanAviation raw archives, recorded aircraft coordinates, recorded input/truth arrays or recorded forecast means are redistributed. The new S5 positions, truth and compact forecasts are wholly synthetic. Full component and internal-state traces remain local for size; original hashes are retained. Mixed-data manuscript snapshots and edit specifications are excluded. Provider data must be obtained from official sources under their terms. No neuromorphic hardware energy, latency or efficiency benefit is claimed. No external funding; no competing interests. Files remain restricted for peer review. The manuscript remains under author review; this archive is not journal submission.

This research candidate adds twelve exact finite-interval certificates for reflexive four-polytopes, an independent integer verifier, and a portable animated certificate explorer. Relative to the supplied Kreuzer–Skarke point-pair census, the maximum shortest descent satisfies 22 ≤ D4 ≤ 346. The prior bound 348 for arbitrary descents is unchanged. items.summary: HIGH-INTEGRITY CARGO TRANSPORT AND CONTROLLED RELEASE IN MICRO/NANOROBOTICS AT THE LIMIT English Introduction This high-density research monograph develops a falsifiable architecture for high-integrity microrobotic cargo transport and controlled release. Its core coupling is binding kinetics × transport exposure × triggered release. Arrival is explicitly separated from delivery: one identified cargo lineage must remain bound through transport, stay below registered shear thermal and chemical exposure limits, avoid premature leakage and cross-contamination, release inside the authorized spatial and temporal window, preserve a cargo-specific functional endpoint, and leave a closed record of residual material and carrier recovery. The central contribution is the Cargo Integrity Passport, a replayable evidence object that binds cargo and carrier identities, initial load, binding calibration, route, exposure waveforms, leakage samples, trigger fields, target masks, released mass, functional assays, contamination panels, unreleased residue, retrieval, abstentions, failures, and final disposition. Thirty physicalized derivations connect directly to 82 chapters, 410 single-page research studies, 200 Research Gates, and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos. When unknown shear pulses, constrictions, sham triggers, second cargo lots, and carrier aging are introduced blindly, the system must lower both premature leakage and nonrelease rather than exchange one failure for the other. Missing mass, destructive triggering, target expansion, and deleted failed cargo reject the claim.

items.summary: we hereby submit our manuscript entitled “Query-Defined Submodels: Publishing Topological Graph Analyses to the Asset Administration Shell” for consideration for publication as an Article in the Industrial Informatics and Digital Twin section of Machines (MDPI).The manuscript proposes a unidirectional pipeline that combines graph-based analysis with standardized information exchange through the Asset Administration Shell (AAS). It addresses a specific limitation of AAS-QL regarding traversal through RelationshipElement endpoints, performs the required topological analysis in a property-graph environment, and exports the selected and potentially derived result as a standards-conformant AAS Submodel. The approach is formalized mathematically by representing the analysis as a mapping from a labelled property graph to a result graph and the export as a second mapping fSrom that result into an AAS Submodel. This makes explicit that the exported extent is query-defined. The proposed architecture is further evaluated analytically with respect to communication and maintenance costs under different production-system configurations.

items.summary: This record contains the replication data and R code for the study “How much does the publication universe matter? Source discontinuities and panel selection in OpenAlex” by Vladislav Bína and Jiří Přibil. The package includes OpenAlex source-by-year counts for 2010–2025 retrieved on 10–11 October 2026, supplementary OpenAlex and Crossref aggregate counts retrieved on 23 October 2026, a provenance-limited earlier archive of annual totals, and twelve annotated illustrative record checks. It also provides eight R scripts, expected numerical results, numerical inputs to the figures, and English documentation. The default workflow reproduces the saved-data analyses offline using base R. It covers publication growth, continuity panels, source turnover, panel-selection timing, population layers, and sensitivity to comparison horizons and endpoints. Version 2.2 was tested with R 4.5.2 on Windows. Data provenance, variable definitions, limitations and reproduction instructions are documented in README.md. Licensing applies by component: bibliographic metadata and factual numerical data/results are provided under CC0 1.0; R code under the MIT License; and original documentation and author annotations under CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE.txt for the exact scopes.

items.summary: The work builds a foundation of physics from a single assumption: everything is a process, and a process is an ideal sine; its centre, the balance, is the observer. Only the square — intensity without phase — passes between levels; from this arise dimensions, the arrow of time, the quantum and the standard. On this basis stable particles are built as standing waves together with their galactic analogues, the initial rules of quantum mechanics and relativity are derived, and the constants are linked to a single number — the speed of light. Agreement with experiment is at the level of a few percent; the model attributes the discrepancies to the imperfection of the standard. Main results The four stable particles (neutrino, electron, neutron, proton) are the four stable states of a standing wave; masses from the speed of light alone: electron +0.7 %, nucleons about −3 % [result given hypotheses]. The Born rule, the randomness of a single outcome, the 2√2 limit in the Bell test, spin ½ and g = 2 [result]. The Lorentz transformation from the “speed budget” c² = v² + v_int², the Klein — Gordon and Schrödinger equations, Schwarzschild gravitational time dilation and the light deflection of 1.75″ [result]. Similarity of the small and the large with the step c⁴: the image of the neutron is the stellar mass of the Milky Way (5.5·10¹⁰ versus (6.1 ± 1.1)·10¹⁰ solar masses) [hypothesis, numerical agreement]. The large end is built by the same logic as the microworld: the construction yields the Hubble constant H₀ = 1/(5c²) ≈ 68.7 km/s/Mpc and the smallest acceleration of galaxies a₀ = 1/(10πc) [result given hypotheses]. The gravitational constant G ≈ c^(−6/5) (0.8 %); the mass of the Universe and the scale of dark energy are expressed through c [hypothesis]. The fine-structure constant has been found as the number 1/α ≈ 4·(c/2π)^(1/5) (0.22 %); its meaning is open [observation]. Limitations: the accuracy is percent-level, not parts per million; the standard and several constants remain open questions. The status of each statement is given in the text. Revision dated 2026-10-24:   The black hole. A black hole is understood as the construction of mass from the large end: particles build mass from the small end, the black hole from the large one. Perception has a limit of tempo: a process whose tempo is below our smallest does not change for us, so the centre is inaccessible, and for us it is space possessing mass and rotation. The horizon is the transition from space into mass; it grows with mass and is not related to the core. The black hole processes volumetric particles into a plane, and the tension of space, when the sizes of galaxies change, again gives birth to particle–antiparticle pairs: the cycle is closed. Only black holes that are analogues of elementary particles are considered. G and α. Both constants have received a geometric reading. Gravity is the work of space in a cross-section, charge is the same work over a closed surface; the surface of a sphere is four times its cross-section, hence the four. Charge is the work of one unpaired half-wave, that is, of one step of the microworld k: 1/α = 4k. G is gravity from the large end: the whole linear path up to the transition and the step linking it with the small end, G = 1/(c·c^(1/5)), without the four. The link of the two constants is G = 4α/((2π)^(1/5)·c). In neutral particles the same transition from flat to volume goes through rotation (support: the magnetic moment of the neutron). items.summary: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.
items.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
